mechanism: Amphotericin B causes renal dysfunction and electrolyte wasting (including phosphate), which impairs the renal conversion of cholecalciferol to its active metabolite calcitriol, while amphotericin B-induced nephrotoxicity decreases vitamin D metabolism and increases hypocalcemia risk.
action: Monitor serum calcium, phosphate, and renal function regularly during concurrent use; consider calcitriol supplementation if active vitamin D metabolite is needed rather than relying on cholecalciferol activation.
